geography.title: A mountain town
paragraphs: Urrao sits in the Andes of western Antioquia, in a valley surrounded by high ridges. Coffee farms climb the slopes toward the Páramo del Sol, where altitude keeps the nights cool.
In general, cool nights and slow ripening give the bean more time to build sugars. That is one reason high-grown Colombian coffees are often clean, sweet and lively in the cup.

varieties.title: Three varieties,

items.name: Chiroso
items.text: The local specialty, valued for a floral, tea-like cup. Rarely planted outside this part of Antioquia.

items.name: Castillo
items.text: Developed in Colombia for resistance to leaf rust, and widely grown across the country.

items.name: Caturra
items.text: A compact, productive plant that Colombian farms have grown for decades.
